text: If you've been out and about this morning, you've caught the good part: mostly clear, mild, that light south breeze. It won't last all day. The showers and rumbles of thunder are due in around midday, roughly noon to 1, then a scattered round through the afternoon into evening, with the atmosphere staying a little unsettled after that too. Nothing soaking, less than a tenth of an inch most spots, but keep the umbrella within reach if you're out this afternoon. The models actually back the wetter read today, with a couple of them putting the odds closer to 40 percent versus the official 30, so I'd lean toward believing you'll see at least one round come through. High near 75, humidity staying reasonable, air quality is good. On the lake, south wind 10 to 15 knots with waves 1 to 3 feet and the same scattered storm risk, so if you're headed out on the water, morning is your better window before things fire up. Showers linger into tonight and Tuesday too before things dry out midweek.
